nodes.name: The martingale term (C.4)
nodes.statement: In this section we complete the proof of Proposition~\ref{th:j2:2}. The arguments are sometimes sketched because analogous to the ones in \cite[Section~6]{j1}. Let $\gamma >3$ and $h\in \Lg{\gamma}$ be fixed. By Definition~\ref{def:integral:gamma} of $\Lg{\gamma}$ there exist a non-negative function $\bar h \in \Lgb{\gamma}$ and a constant $a\in[0,\infty)$ such that $|h(x,y)| \leq \bar h(x) e^{a |y-x|}$. In this section $\bar h$ and $a$ are fixed. \\ Let us also recall some notation: let $\bfH{}$ the functional in \eqref{eq:muX}, $Q^\sigma$ the semigroup in~\eqref{eq:def:semig}, $\bfG{h}$ in~\eqref{eq:kappa}, $\mathcal{Q}$ in~\eqref{eq:cQ} and its limit $\mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y}$ in~\eqref{eq:cQ:limit} (see Lemma~\ref{lem:cQ:conv}), and $\mathbb{L}$ in~\eqref{function:G}. For all $n\in \mathbb{N}$ the $(\mathcal{F}_{\lfloor n t\rfloor /n})_{t\in [0,1]}$-martingale $\mathcal{M}^n$ in \eqref{eq:mv} rewrites as $ { \mathcal{M}^n_t = \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor n t \rfloor} \chi^n_k} $ where \begin{equation} \begin{split} \chi^n_k := n^{-\frac14} & \left( h(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}, \sqrt{n} Y_{k/n} ) - \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle \, \sqrt{n}(L_{k/n}(Y) - L_{(k-1)/n}(Y)) \right) \\ + \, & n^{-\frac14} \left(\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{k/n}) - \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) \right)\!. \end{split} \end{equation} Now it remains to prove Items~\ref{th:j2:item1:2}-\ref{th:j2:item4:2} in Proposition~\ref{th:j2:2}. \subsubsection{Proof of Item~\ref{th:j2:item1:2} in Proposition~\ref{th:j2:2} } It follows from scaling property \eqref{Yscaling} and Lemma~\ref{lem:conv:hatg}. For all $n\in \mathbb{N}$, $k\in \{1, \ldots, \lfloor n \rfloor \}$, the scaling property \eqref{Yscaling}, Lemma~\ref{lem:conv:hatg} and \eqref{eq:cQ} ensure that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \chi_k^n | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & = n^{-\frac14} \left( \bfG{h}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) + \int_{-\infty}^\infty \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(y) q_\sigma(1, \sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}, y) \,\mathrm{d} y - \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n})\right) \\ & = n^{-\frac14} \left(Q^\sigma_1 \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) - \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n})\right)=0. \end{split} \end{equation} \subsubsection{Proof of Item~\ref{th:j2:item2:2} in Proposition~\ref{th:j2:2}} Let $t\in [0,1]$ be fixed. {\it First step:} It can be easily shown that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \sqrt n \mathbb{E}\!\left[ (\chi_k^n)^2 | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & = f_{n}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) + (\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle)^2 \Lm{1}{2}{\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}} - 2 \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle h_n(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) \end{split} \end{equation} where $f_n$ and $h_n$ are given by $ f_n(x) := \bfH {h^2}(x) + 2 \bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}} (x) + g_n(x) $ and $ h_n(x):= \Lm{h(x, \cdot)}{1}{x} + \Lm{\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}{1}{x}, $ with $ g_n(x):=Q^\sigma_1\left( ( \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0} )^2 \right) (x) - \left(\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(x)\right)^2 $. In fact first note that, by \eqref{function:G:equal}, for all $k =1, \ldots, {\lfloor n t \rfloor}$ it holds that \begin{equation} h_n(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k-1}{n}})= \sqrt{n} \mathbb{E}\Big[ (h(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k-1}{n}}, \sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k}{n}}) + \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k}{n}}) ) (L_{\frac{k}{n}}(Y) - L_{\frac{k-1}n}(Y)) | \mathcal{F}_{\frac{k-1}n}\Big] . \end{equation} Let us now consider $f_n$. Clearly $f_n$ have to be the sum of all remaining terms and it has to have the desired form. This follows from the fact that the scaling property~\eqref{Yscaling} and equation~\eqref{eq:cQ} ensure that $\mathbb{E}\Big[ (\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{k/n}))^2 | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\Big] = Q^\sigma_1 ( (\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{k/n}))^2 ). $ but also $\mathbb{E}\Big[ \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{k/n}) | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\Big] = \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(\sqrt n Y_{(k-1)/n})$ which, together with the definition of $\bfG{h}$ in \eqref{eq:kappa}, \eqref{function:G:equal}, and the fact that $ \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) = \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) - \bfG{h}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) $ show that $\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n})$ can be rewritten as \begin{equation} \begin{split} \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k-1}{n}}) = \mathbb{E}\Big[ h(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k-1}n}, \sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k}{n}}) + \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k}n}) -\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle \sqrt{n} ( L_{\frac{k}n}(Y) - L_{\frac{k-1}n}(Y) ) | \mathcal{F}_{\frac{k-1}n}\Big] . \end{split} \end{equation} The proof of the first step is thus completed. {\it Second step:} It follows from applying Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1b:j1} to the constant sequence of functions $\Lm{1}{2}{\cdot}$ that $ \frac1{\sqrt n} \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor n t \rfloor} \Lm{1}{2}{\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}} \convp[n\to\infty] \frac{2 \sigma_- \sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+} \frac{8}{3 \sqrt{2 \pi}} L_t(Y). $ The fact that the assumptions of the proposition (i.e.~$\Lm{1}{2}{\cdot} \in \Lgb{2}$) are satisfied and $\langle \lambda_\sigma , \Lm{1}{2}{\cdot} \rangle = \frac{2 \sigma_- \sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+} \frac{8}{3 \sqrt{2 \pi}}$ follows from the fact that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[ \left( L_1(W)\right)^2\right]= 1$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:G}. In the two final steps, we want to apply Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1b:j1} to the sequences $f_n$ and $h_n$. {\em Third step:\/} We show that $ \frac1{\sqrt n} \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor n t \rfloor} f_n (\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) \convp[n\to\infty] \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH {h^2} + 2 \bfH{h, \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} } \rangle L_t(Y). $ applying Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1b:j1}. To do so we check that the sequence $f_n$ satisfies \eqref{eq:j1:4.2} and that $ \lim_{n\to\infty}\langle \lambda_\sigma , f_n \rangle=\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH {h^2} + 2 \bfH{h, \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} } \rangle $. The fact that $\lim_{n\to\infty} \langle \lambda_\sigma , g_n \rangle$=0 follows from the fact that $\lambda_\sigma$ is a stationary measure, inequality~\eqref{eq:cQ:prop1} with $\zeta=\gamma-1 >2$, and inequality~\eqref{eq:cQ:prop2}. Note that $ \bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}= \bfH{h, \bfG{h}}+\bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}}. $ Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa} (in particular the fact that $\bfG{h}$ is bounded) ensures that there exists a constant $K\in (0,\infty)$ such that $ |\bfH{h, \bfG{h}}(x)| \leq K \bar h(x) . $ By \eqref{eq:cQ:prop3} there exists constants $K_1,K_2\in (0,\infty)$ (all depending on $\sigma_\pm$ and $K_2$ depending also on the constant $a\in [0,\infty)$) such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} |\bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}}(x)| & \leq K_1 \bar h(x) \left( \int_{-\infty}^\infty (1+|x| \ind{[-x,x]}(y)+ |y| \ind{\mathbb{R}\setminus[-x,x]}(y)) e^{a |y-x|} q_\sigma (1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y \right) \\ & \leq K_2 \bar h(x) (1+|x|). \end{split} \end{equation} The fact that $h\in \Lg{\gamma}\subseteq \Lg{2}$ ensures that $\bar h \in \Lgb{1}$ (by Lemma~\ref{lem:link:theorems}) and so $\bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}} \in \mathcal{L}^1$. Hence, dominated convergence and Lemma~\ref{lem:cQ:conv} show that $ \lim_{n\to\infty}\langle \lambda_\sigma , f_n \rangle=\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH {h^2} + 2 \bfH{h, \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} } \rangle $. Let us now show that $f_n$ satisfies equation \eqref{eq:j1:4.2}. By~Lemma~\ref{lem:link:theorems}, $\bfH {h^2} \in \Lgb{2}$. \\ Let us explore the contribution to \eqref{eq:j1:4.2} of the other parts of $f_n$. Let us first consider $ \bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}= \bfH{h, \bfG{h}}+\bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}}. $ Above we saw that $|\bfH{h, \bfG{h}}|\leq K\bar h$ with $K$ non negative constant. Cauchy-Schwarz inequality implies that \begin{equation} ( \bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}}(x) )^2 \leq \int_{-\infty}^\infty h(x,y)^2 q_\sigma (1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y \int_{-\infty}^\infty (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}(y))^2 q_\sigma (1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y. \end{equation} It can be easily shown that the first factor is uniformly bounded by a finite constant. And by \eqref{eq:cQ:prop2} (taking $\zeta = \gamma-1>2$) there exist constants $K_1,K_2\in (0,\infty)$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} Q^\sigma_1 \left( (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0})^2 \right) & = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}(y))^2 q_\sigma (1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y \\ & \leq K_1 \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{(\log n)^2 q_\sigma (1,x,y)}{(1+|y n^{-\frac18}/\sigma(y)|^{\gamma-1})^2} \,\mathrm{d} y \leq \frac{ K_2 (\log (n))^2}{1+|x n^{-\frac18}/\sigma(x)|^{2(\gamma-1)}}. \end{split} \end{equation} The last inequality are consequences of the upper bound for the transition density of OBM $ q_\sigma(1,x,y) \leq \frac{\left(1+\left|\frac{\sigma_--\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right|\right)}{\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma(y)} e^{-\frac12(\frac{y}{\sigma(y)}-\frac{x}{\sigma(x)})^2} $ and of \cite[Lemma~3.2]{j1} (or some computations). Therefore $ \bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}(x) \leq K \left(\bar h(x) + \frac{ \log (n)}{1+|x n^{-\frac18}/\sigma(x)|^{\gamma-1}} \right)\!.$ Finally we consider the auxiliary function $g_n$: note that $ |g_n|(x) \leq Q^\sigma_1 ( 2 (\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0})^2 + 2 (\bfG{h})^2)(x) + 2 (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(x))^2 + 2(\bfG{h}(x))^2. $ Inequality~\eqref{eq:cQ:prop2} and inequality~\eqref{eq:recicle} imply that $Q^\sigma_1 \left( (\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0})^2 \right) (x)+ (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(x))^2 \leq \frac{ K (\log (n))^2}{1+|x n^{-\frac18}/\sigma(x)|^{2(\gamma-1)}}$ for some non negative constant $K$. Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa}, the fact that $\gamma \geq 2$ and Item~\ref{item2bis:semig:estim} of Lemma~\ref{lem:semig:estim} yields $(\bfG{h})^2\leq K \bfG{h}$ and $ Q^\sigma_1 \left((\bfG{h})^2\right) (x) \leq K (e^{-x^2/2} + \frac{1}{1+({|x|}/{\sigma(x)})^\gamma}) $ for some non-negative constant $K$. Combining all terms yields that $f_n$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:j1:4.2}. (Here we used the fact that $\gamma \geq 3$ and $\eta=1/4<1/3$ in the definition of $\mathcal{Q}$.) {\em Fourth step:\/} We show that $ \frac1{\sqrt n} \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor n t \rfloor} h_n(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) \convp[n\to\infty] c_h L_t(Y) $ applying Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1b:j1}, where $ 2 \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle c_h:= - K_h + \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH {h^2} + 2 \bfH{h,\mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} } \rangle + \frac{ 2 \sigma_- \sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+} \frac{8}{3 \sqrt{2\pi}} (\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle)^2 $. To do so we check that the sequence $h_n$ satisfies \eqref{eq:j1:4.2} and that $ \lim_{n\to\infty} \langle \lambda_\sigma , h_n \rangle=c_h $. Inequality~\eqref{eq:cQ:prop3}, the fact that $\bfG{h}$ is bounded (see Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa}), the fact that \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}\!\left[ L_1(W) (1 + |W_1|+ e^{a \sigma(W_1) |W_1|} \ind{\{\sigma(W_1)\in \mathbb{R}\}}) \right]<\infty \end{equation} (see the joint density of BM and its local time~\eqref{eq:BMl}), boundedness of $\bar h$, and the change of variable $s= \frac{x^2}{ (\sigma(x))^2 t}$ show that there exists $K\in (0,\infty)$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & |\Lm{h(x,\cdot)}{1}{x}| + |\Lm{\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}{1}{x}| \leq 2 K |x| e^{-\frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2}} \in \mathcal{L}^1. \end{split} \end{equation} Hence dominated convergence, and Lemma~\ref{lem:cQ:conv} demonstrates that $\lim_{n\to\infty} \langle \lambda_\sigma , \Lm{\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}{1}{\cdot} \rangle = \langle \lambda_\sigma , \Lm{ \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} }{1}{\cdot} \rangle$. Moreover the latter inequalities ensure also that $h_n$ satisfy \eqref{eq:j1:4.2}. Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:G} allows us to rewrite $c_h:= \langle \lambda_\sigma , \Lm{ h(\cdot,) }{1}{\cdot} \rangle + \langle \lambda_\sigma , \Lm{ \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} }{1}{\cdot} \rangle$ as \begin{equation}\begin{split} & c_h = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{(\sigma_- + \sigma_+)}{2\sigma_-\sigma_+} \int_0^1 \sqrt{\frac{1}t-1} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \int_0^\infty \rho_1^\sigma(y,\ell) \ell \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} (y \sqrt{1-t}) \,\mathrm{d} \ell \,\mathrm{d} y \,\mathrm{d} t \\ & \qquad + \int_{-\infty}^\infty \int_0^1 \int_{-\infty}^\infty \int_0^\infty \frac{|x| e^{-\frac{x^2}{2 (\sigma(x))^2}}}{\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma(x)} \sqrt{\frac{1}t-1} \rho_1^\sigma(y,\ell) \ell h(x \sqrt{t},y \sqrt{1-t}) \,\mathrm{d} \ell \,\mathrm{d} y \,\mathrm{d} t \lambda_\sigma(\!\,\mathrm{d} x) \end{split}\end{equation} where $\rho_1^\sigma$ is the joint density of a standard OBM and its local time at time $1$ (given in \eqref{eq:OBMl}). This expression can be easily checked to be the desired expression for $c_h$. \subsubsection{Proof of Item~\ref{th:j2:item3:2} in Proposition~\ref{th:j2:2}} Let $t\in [0,1]$ be fixed. {\it First step:} Let us show that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[\chi_k^n (Y_{k/n} - Y_{(k-1)/n}) | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & = \frac1{\sqrt n} \left( n^{-\frac14} f_1(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) + g_{n}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) + \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle n^{-\frac14} f_2(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n})\right) \end{split} \end{equation} where $f_1,f_2,g_n$ are given by \begin{equation} \begin{split} f_1(x)& := \int_{-\infty}^\infty (h(x,y)+\bfG{h}(y)) (y-x) q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y , \ f_2(x):= x \Lm{1}{1}{x}, \ \text{and} \\ g_n(x) & := n^{-\frac14} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}(y) (y-x) q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y. \end{split} \end{equation} Throughout the proof of this step let $\mathbb{Id} \colon x\mapsto x$ denote the identity function. It follows from \eqref{eq:chi:nk}, the fact that $Y$ is a martingale, \eqref{function:G:equal}, and the scaling property~\eqref{Yscaling} that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & n^{\frac34} \, \mathbb{E}\!\left[\chi_k^n (Y_{k/n} - Y_{(k-1)/n}) | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & = f_1(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) + \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle f_2(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) - \Lm{ \mathbb{Id} }{1}{\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}} ) + n^{1/4}g_n(\sqrt{n}Y_{(k-1)/n}). \end{split} \end{equation} The proof of this step is completed if $ \Lm{ \mathbb{Id} }{1}{\cdot} =0$. This equality follows from the fact that for a standard BM, say $W$, it holds that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[ L_1(W) W_1 \right]=0$ and from Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:G}. In the next steps we want to check that Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1a:j1} can be applied to the sequences $n^{-\frac14} f_1$, $n^{-\frac14} f_2$ and $g_n$. {\it Second step:} We show that $f_1$ is bounded and integrable: $f_1\in \Lgb{0}$. The proof follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa}, and Item~\ref{item2bis:semig:estim} in Lemma~\ref{lem:semig:estim}. In this proof the fact that $\gamma>3$ is strongly used. The fact that $h\in \Lg{\gamma}\subseteq \Lg{3}$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa} ensure that $\bar h$ and $\bfG{h}$ are in $\Lgb{2}$. This, Cauchy-Schwarz, the fact that $ \left(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (y-x)^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right) \leq \sigma_-^2 \ind{\{\sigma_-\in\mathbb{R}\}} +\sigma_+^2 \ind{\{\sigma_+\in\mathbb{R}\}} $, and the fact that that $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (\bfG{h}(y))^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y = Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)$ yield \begin{equation} \begin{split} |f_1(x)| & \leq \bar h(x) \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{a |y-x|} |y-x| q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y + \sqrt{\sigma_-^2 \ind{\{\sigma_-\in\mathbb{R}\}} +\sigma_+^2 \ind{\{\sigma_+\in\mathbb{R}\}}} \left( |Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)| \right)^{\!1/2}. \end{split} \end{equation} By Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa} $\bfG{h}$ is bounded, i.e.~there exists $K\in (0,\infty)$ such that $\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}}|\bfG{h}(x)|\leq K$ and $\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfG{h} \rangle=0 $, and so $ | \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfG{h}^2 \rangle | \leq K | \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfG{h} \rangle | =0. $ And so Item~\ref{item2bis:semig:estim} in Lemma~\ref{lem:semig:estim} implies, up to increase the constant $K\in [1,\infty)$, that \begin{equation} |Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)| \leq K \frac{1}{1+|x/\sigma(x)|^{\gamma-1}} + K \frac1{\sqrt{2 \pi}} e^{-\frac{x^2}{2 (\sigma(x))^2 }} \leq 2 K^2 \frac{1}{(1+|x/\sigma(x)|^{\frac{\gamma-1}{2}})^2} . \end{equation} Since $\gamma >3 $ it holds that $\left( |Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)| \right)^{\!\frac12}\in \Lgb{0}$ and so $|f_1|\in \Lgb{0}$. {\it Third step:} The fact that $f_2$ is bounded and integrable follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:G}. This and the change of variable $s \mapsto r= \frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2 s}$ show that there exists a positive constant $K$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} f_2(x) & = \left(\frac{2 \sigma_-\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right)^{\! 2} \frac{x |x|}{\sigma(x)} \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \frac{L_1(W)}{\sigma(W_1)} \right] \int_0^1 \frac{\sqrt{1-s}}{\sqrt{2\pi} s^\frac32} e^{-\frac{x^2}{2 (\sigma(x))^2 s}} \! \,\mathrm{d} s \\ & = \left(\frac{2 \sigma_-\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right)^{\! 2} \frac{x |x|}{\sigma(x)} \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \frac{L_1(W)}{\sigma(W_1)} \right] \int_{\frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2}}^\infty \frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}} \sqrt{\frac{(\sigma(x))^2}{x^2}-\frac1r} e^{-\frac{r}{2}} \frac1{\sqrt{r}}\! \,\mathrm{d} r \ \ind{\{\sigma(x)\in \mathbb{R}\}} \\ & \leq \left(\frac{2 \sigma_-\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right)^{\! 2} \frac{|x| \mathbb{E}\!\left[L_1(W)\right] }{\min\{\sigma_-,\sigma_+\}} \int_{\frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2}}^\infty \frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{r}{2}} \frac1{\sqrt{r}}\! \,\mathrm{d} r \ \ind{\{\sigma(x)\in \mathbb{R}\}} \leq K e^{-\frac{x^2}{4(\sigma(x))^2}} \in \Lgb{0}. \end{split} \end{equation} In the last inequality we used that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[ L_1(W) \right] \in [0,\infty)$. This step is thus completed. {\it Fourth step:} We prove that $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |g_n(x)| \,\mathrm{d} x$ and $\frac1{\sqrt{n}} g_n(\sqrt{n} x)$ converge to 0. Cauchy-Schwarz inequality ensures \begin{equation} \begin{split} |g_n(x)|^2 & \leq n^{-1/2} \left( \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}(y))^2 q_\sigma (1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right) \left(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (y-x)^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right). \end{split} \end{equation} Note that $ \left(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (y-x)^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right) \leq \sigma_-^2 \ind{\{\sigma_-\in \mathbb{R}\}} +\sigma_+^2 \ind{\{\sigma_+\in \mathbb{R}\}} $ and inequality~\eqref{eq:recicle} yield that there exists a constant $K\in (0,\infty)$ depending on $\gamma$ and $\sigma_\pm$ such that $ |g_n(x)| \leq \frac{n^{-\frac14} K_2 \log (n)}{1+|x n^{-\frac18}/\sigma(x)|^{\gamma-1}}. $ In the last steps we proved that Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1a:j1} can be applied and this completes the proof. \subsubsection{Proof of Item~\ref{th:j2:item4:2} in Proposition~\ref{th:j2:2}} Let $\varepsilon \in (0,\infty)$ be fixed. For every $k$, H\"older's inequality and Markov's inequality show \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[ |\chi_k^n|^2 \ind{\{|\chi_k^n|\geq \varepsilon \}}| \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \leq \mathbb{E}\!\left[ |\chi_k^n|^{5} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \varepsilon^{-3} . \end{split} \end{equation} The fact that $h\in \Lg{\gamma}\subseteq \Lg{0}$ ensures that $\bar h$ is bounded and integrable. This combined with Jensen's inequality and \eqref{eq:cQ:prop4} ensures that $\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}} \bar h(x) + |\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle| $ is bounded by a constant $K\in (0,\infty)$ and for all $n\in \mathbb{N}\setminus\{0,1,2,3\}$ it holds that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[ |\chi_k^n|^{5} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \leq 4^{4} n^{-\frac{5}{4}} K^{5} \Big( \mathbb{E}\!\left[ e^{5 a \sqrt n | Y_{k/n} - Y_{(k-1)/n}|} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & \quad \qquad + \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \left(\sqrt{n}|L_{k/n}(Y) - L_{(k-1)/n}(Y)| \right)^{5} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] + (\log n)^{5} \Big). \end{split} \end{equation} The fact that density of the OBM has a Gaussian behavior together with the scaling property~\eqref{Yscaling} ensure that $ \mathbb{E}\!\left[ e^{5 a \sqrt n | Y_{k/n} - Y_{(k-1)/n}|} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{5 a |y-x|} q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y $ is bounded. By \eqref{function:G} and Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:G} we can show, similarly to the third step of the proof of Item~\ref{th:j2:item3}, that there exist constants $K_1,K_2 \in (0,\infty)$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \left(\sqrt{n}|L_{k/n}(Y) - L_{(k-1)/n}(Y)| \right)^{5} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] = \Lm {1}{5}{\sqrt{n}Y_{(k-1)/n}} \\ & \leq K_1 \int_0^1 \frac{(1-t)^{\frac52}}{\sqrt{2 \pi} t^{\frac32}} \frac{\sqrt{n}|Y_{(k-1)/n}|}{\sigma(Y_{(k-1)/n})} e^{-\frac{n (Y_{(k-1)/n})^2}{2 (\sigma(Y_{(k-1)/n})) t } } \,\mathrm{d} t \leq K_2. \end{split} \end{equation} We conclude that there exists a constant $K\in (0,\infty)$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \sum_{k=1}^n \mathbb{E}\!\left[ |\chi_k^n|^2 \ind{\{|\chi_k^n|\geq \varepsilon \}}| \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \leq n K n^{-\frac54} \log(n) \varepsilon^{-3} \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{} 0. \end{split} \end{equation}
nodes.section: C.4 Dealing with the martingale term
nodes.statement_short: Verify items (i)-(iv) for the increments $\chi^n_k$.

nodes.name: Increments $\chi^n_k$
nodes.statement: In this section we complete the proof of Proposition~\ref{th:j2:2}. The arguments are sometimes sketched because analogous to the ones in \cite[Section~6]{j1}. Let $\gamma >3$ and $h\in \Lg{\gamma}$ be fixed. By Definition~\ref{def:integral:gamma} of $\Lg{\gamma}$ there exist a non-negative function $\bar h \in \Lgb{\gamma}$ and a constant $a\in[0,\infty)$ such that $|h(x,y)| \leq \bar h(x) e^{a |y-x|}$. In this section $\bar h$ and $a$ are fixed. \\ Let us also recall some notation: let $\bfH{}$ the functional in \eqref{eq:muX}, $Q^\sigma$ the semigroup in~\eqref{eq:def:semig}, $\bfG{h}$ in~\eqref{eq:kappa}, $\mathcal{Q}$ in~\eqref{eq:cQ} and its limit $\mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y}$ in~\eqref{eq:cQ:limit} (see Lemma~\ref{lem:cQ:conv}), and $\mathbb{L}$ in~\eqref{function:G}. For all $n\in \mathbb{N}$ the $(\mathcal{F}_{\lfloor n t\rfloor /n})_{t\in [0,1]}$-martingale $\mathcal{M}^n$ in \eqref{eq:mv} rewrites as $ { \mathcal{M}^n_t = \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor n t \rfloor} \chi^n_k} $ where \begin{equation} \begin{split} \chi^n_k := n^{-\frac14} & \left( h(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}, \sqrt{n} Y_{k/n} ) - \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle \, \sqrt{n}(L_{k/n}(Y) - L_{(k-1)/n}(Y)) \right) \\ + \, & n^{-\frac14} \left(\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{k/n}) - \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) \right)\!. \end{split} \end{equation} Now it remains to prove Items~\ref{th:j2:item1:2}-\ref{th:j2:item4:2} in Proposition~\ref{th:j2:2}.
nodes.section: C.4 Dealing with the martingale term
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $\mathcal{M}^n$ as a sum of increments $\chi^n_k$.

nodes.name: Equation (C.20): Martingale increments $\chi^n_k$
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \chi^n_k := n^{-\frac14} & \left( h(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}, \sqrt{n} Y_{k/n} ) - \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle \, \sqrt{n}(L_{k/n}(Y) - L_{(k-1)/n}(Y)) \right) \\ + \, & n^{-\frac14} \left(\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{k/n}) - \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) \right)\!. \end{split}
nodes.section: C.4 Dealing with the martingale term
nodes.label: eq:chi:nk

nodes.name: Item (i)
nodes.statement: It follows from scaling property \eqref{Yscaling} and Lemma~\ref{lem:conv:hatg}. For all $n\in \mathbb{N}$, $k\in \{1, \ldots, \lfloor n \rfloor \}$, the scaling property \eqref{Yscaling}, Lemma~\ref{lem:conv:hatg} and \eqref{eq:cQ} ensure that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \chi_k^n | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & = n^{-\frac14} \left( \bfG{h}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) + \int_{-\infty}^\infty \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(y) q_\sigma(1, \sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}, y) \,\mathrm{d} y - \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n})\right) \\ & = n^{-\frac14} \left(Q^\sigma_1 \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) - \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n})\right)=0. \end{split} \end{equation}
nodes.section: C.4 Dealing with the martingale term
nodes.statement_short: Conditional means vanish by scaling, Lemma 8 and (C.10).

nodes.name: Equation (C.21)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \chi_k^n | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & = n^{-\frac14} \left( \bfG{h}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) + \int_{-\infty}^\infty \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(y) q_\sigma(1, \sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}, y) \,\mathrm{d} y - \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n})\right) \\ & = n^{-\frac14} \left(Q^\sigma_1 \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) - \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n})\right)=0. \end{split}
nodes.section: C.4.1 Proof of Item~th:j2:item1:2 in Proposition~4

nodes.name: Item (ii)
nodes.statement: Let $t\in [0,1]$ be fixed. {\it First step:} It can be easily shown that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \sqrt n \mathbb{E}\!\left[ (\chi_k^n)^2 | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & = f_{n}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) + (\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle)^2 \Lm{1}{2}{\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}} - 2 \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle h_n(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) \end{split} \end{equation} where $f_n$ and $h_n$ are given by $ f_n(x) := \bfH {h^2}(x) + 2 \bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}} (x) + g_n(x) $ and $ h_n(x):= \Lm{h(x, \cdot)}{1}{x} + \Lm{\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}{1}{x}, $ with $ g_n(x):=Q^\sigma_1\left( ( \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0} )^2 \right) (x) - \left(\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(x)\right)^2 $. In fact first note that, by \eqref{function:G:equal}, for all $k =1, \ldots, {\lfloor n t \rfloor}$ it holds that \begin{equation} h_n(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k-1}{n}})= \sqrt{n} \mathbb{E}\Big[ (h(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k-1}{n}}, \sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k}{n}}) + \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k}{n}}) ) (L_{\frac{k}{n}}(Y) - L_{\frac{k-1}n}(Y)) | \mathcal{F}_{\frac{k-1}n}\Big] . \end{equation} Let us now consider $f_n$. Clearly $f_n$ have to be the sum of all remaining terms and it has to have the desired form. This follows from the fact that the scaling property~\eqref{Yscaling} and equation~\eqref{eq:cQ} ensure that $\mathbb{E}\Big[ (\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{k/n}))^2 | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\Big] = Q^\sigma_1 ( (\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{k/n}))^2 ). $ but also $\mathbb{E}\Big[ \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{k/n}) | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\Big] = \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(\sqrt n Y_{(k-1)/n})$ which, together with the definition of $\bfG{h}$ in \eqref{eq:kappa}, \eqref{function:G:equal}, and the fact that $ \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) = \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) - \bfG{h}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) $ show that $\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n})$ can be rewritten as \begin{equation} \begin{split} \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k-1}{n}}) = \mathbb{E}\Big[ h(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k-1}n}, \sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k}{n}}) + \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k}n}) -\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle \sqrt{n} ( L_{\frac{k}n}(Y) - L_{\frac{k-1}n}(Y) ) | \mathcal{F}_{\frac{k-1}n}\Big] . \end{split} \end{equation} The proof of the first step is thus completed. {\it Second step:} It follows from applying Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1b:j1} to the constant sequence of functions $\Lm{1}{2}{\cdot}$ that $ \frac1{\sqrt n} \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor n t \rfloor} \Lm{1}{2}{\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}} \convp[n\to\infty] \frac{2 \sigma_- \sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+} \frac{8}{3 \sqrt{2 \pi}} L_t(Y). $ The fact that the assumptions of the proposition (i.e.~$\Lm{1}{2}{\cdot} \in \Lgb{2}$) are satisfied and $\langle \lambda_\sigma , \Lm{1}{2}{\cdot} \rangle = \frac{2 \sigma_- \sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+} \frac{8}{3 \sqrt{2 \pi}}$ follows from the fact that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[ \left( L_1(W)\right)^2\right]= 1$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:G}. In the two final steps, we want to apply Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1b:j1} to the sequences $f_n$ and $h_n$. {\em Third step:\/} We show that $ \frac1{\sqrt n} \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor n t \rfloor} f_n (\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) \convp[n\to\infty] \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH {h^2} + 2 \bfH{h, \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} } \rangle L_t(Y). $ applying Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1b:j1}. To do so we check that the sequence $f_n$ satisfies \eqref{eq:j1:4.2} and that $ \lim_{n\to\infty}\langle \lambda_\sigma , f_n \rangle=\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH {h^2} + 2 \bfH{h, \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} } \rangle $. The fact that $\lim_{n\to\infty} \langle \lambda_\sigma , g_n \rangle$=0 follows from the fact that $\lambda_\sigma$ is a stationary measure, inequality~\eqref{eq:cQ:prop1} with $\zeta=\gamma-1 >2$, and inequality~\eqref{eq:cQ:prop2}. Note that $ \bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}= \bfH{h, \bfG{h}}+\bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}}. $ Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa} (in particular the fact that $\bfG{h}$ is bounded) ensures that there exists a constant $K\in (0,\infty)$ such that $ |\bfH{h, \bfG{h}}(x)| \leq K \bar h(x) . $ By \eqref{eq:cQ:prop3} there exists constants $K_1,K_2\in (0,\infty)$ (all depending on $\sigma_\pm$ and $K_2$ depending also on the constant $a\in [0,\infty)$) such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} |\bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}}(x)| & \leq K_1 \bar h(x) \left( \int_{-\infty}^\infty (1+|x| \ind{[-x,x]}(y)+ |y| \ind{\mathbb{R}\setminus[-x,x]}(y)) e^{a |y-x|} q_\sigma (1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y \right) \\ & \leq K_2 \bar h(x) (1+|x|). \end{split} \end{equation} The fact that $h\in \Lg{\gamma}\subseteq \Lg{2}$ ensures that $\bar h \in \Lgb{1}$ (by Lemma~\ref{lem:link:theorems}) and so $\bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}} \in \mathcal{L}^1$. Hence, dominated convergence and Lemma~\ref{lem:cQ:conv} show that $ \lim_{n\to\infty}\langle \lambda_\sigma , f_n \rangle=\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH {h^2} + 2 \bfH{h, \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} } \rangle $. Let us now show that $f_n$ satisfies equation \eqref{eq:j1:4.2}. By~Lemma~\ref{lem:link:theorems}, $\bfH {h^2} \in \Lgb{2}$. \\ Let us explore the contribution to \eqref{eq:j1:4.2} of the other parts of $f_n$. Let us first consider $ \bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}= \bfH{h, \bfG{h}}+\bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}}. $ Above we saw that $|\bfH{h, \bfG{h}}|\leq K\bar h$ with $K$ non negative constant. Cauchy-Schwarz inequality implies that \begin{equation} ( \bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}}(x) )^2 \leq \int_{-\infty}^\infty h(x,y)^2 q_\sigma (1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y \int_{-\infty}^\infty (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}(y))^2 q_\sigma (1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y. \end{equation} It can be easily shown that the first factor is uniformly bounded by a finite constant. And by \eqref{eq:cQ:prop2} (taking $\zeta = \gamma-1>2$) there exist constants $K_1,K_2\in (0,\infty)$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} Q^\sigma_1 \left( (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0})^2 \right) & = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}(y))^2 q_\sigma (1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y \\ & \leq K_1 \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{(\log n)^2 q_\sigma (1,x,y)}{(1+|y n^{-\frac18}/\sigma(y)|^{\gamma-1})^2} \,\mathrm{d} y \leq \frac{ K_2 (\log (n))^2}{1+|x n^{-\frac18}/\sigma(x)|^{2(\gamma-1)}}. \end{split} \end{equation} The last inequality are consequences of the upper bound for the transition density of OBM $ q_\sigma(1,x,y) \leq \frac{\left(1+\left|\frac{\sigma_--\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right|\right)}{\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma(y)} e^{-\frac12(\frac{y}{\sigma(y)}-\frac{x}{\sigma(x)})^2} $ and of \cite[Lemma~3.2]{j1} (or some computations). Therefore $ \bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}(x) \leq K \left(\bar h(x) + \frac{ \log (n)}{1+|x n^{-\frac18}/\sigma(x)|^{\gamma-1}} \right)\!.$ Finally we consider the auxiliary function $g_n$: note that $ |g_n|(x) \leq Q^\sigma_1 ( 2 (\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0})^2 + 2 (\bfG{h})^2)(x) + 2 (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(x))^2 + 2(\bfG{h}(x))^2. $ Inequality~\eqref{eq:cQ:prop2} and inequality~\eqref{eq:recicle} imply that $Q^\sigma_1 \left( (\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0})^2 \right) (x)+ (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(x))^2 \leq \frac{ K (\log (n))^2}{1+|x n^{-\frac18}/\sigma(x)|^{2(\gamma-1)}}$ for some non negative constant $K$. Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa}, the fact that $\gamma \geq 2$ and Item~\ref{item2bis:semig:estim} of Lemma~\ref{lem:semig:estim} yields $(\bfG{h})^2\leq K \bfG{h}$ and $ Q^\sigma_1 \left((\bfG{h})^2\right) (x) \leq K (e^{-x^2/2} + \frac{1}{1+({|x|}/{\sigma(x)})^\gamma}) $ for some non-negative constant $K$. Combining all terms yields that $f_n$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:j1:4.2}. (Here we used the fact that $\gamma \geq 3$ and $\eta=1/4<1/3$ in the definition of $\mathcal{Q}$.) {\em Fourth step:\/} We show that $ \frac1{\sqrt n} \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor n t \rfloor} h_n(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) \convp[n\to\infty] c_h L_t(Y) $ applying Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1b:j1}, where $ 2 \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle c_h:= - K_h + \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH {h^2} + 2 \bfH{h,\mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} } \rangle + \frac{ 2 \sigma_- \sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+} \frac{8}{3 \sqrt{2\pi}} (\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle)^2 $. To do so we check that the sequence $h_n$ satisfies \eqref{eq:j1:4.2} and that $ \lim_{n\to\infty} \langle \lambda_\sigma , h_n \rangle=c_h $. Inequality~\eqref{eq:cQ:prop3}, the fact that $\bfG{h}$ is bounded (see Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa}), the fact that \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}\!\left[ L_1(W) (1 + |W_1|+ e^{a \sigma(W_1) |W_1|} \ind{\{\sigma(W_1)\in \mathbb{R}\}}) \right]<\infty \end{equation} (see the joint density of BM and its local time~\eqref{eq:BMl}), boundedness of $\bar h$, and the change of variable $s= \frac{x^2}{ (\sigma(x))^2 t}$ show that there exists $K\in (0,\infty)$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & |\Lm{h(x,\cdot)}{1}{x}| + |\Lm{\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}{1}{x}| \leq 2 K |x| e^{-\frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2}} \in \mathcal{L}^1. \end{split} \end{equation} Hence dominated convergence, and Lemma~\ref{lem:cQ:conv} demonstrates that $\lim_{n\to\infty} \langle \lambda_\sigma , \Lm{\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}{1}{\cdot} \rangle = \langle \lambda_\sigma , \Lm{ \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} }{1}{\cdot} \rangle$. Moreover the latter inequalities ensure also that $h_n$ satisfy \eqref{eq:j1:4.2}. Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:G} allows us to rewrite $c_h:= \langle \lambda_\sigma , \Lm{ h(\cdot,) }{1}{\cdot} \rangle + \langle \lambda_\sigma , \Lm{ \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} }{1}{\cdot} \rangle$ as \begin{equation}\begin{split} & c_h = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{(\sigma_- + \sigma_+)}{2\sigma_-\sigma_+} \int_0^1 \sqrt{\frac{1}t-1} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \int_0^\infty \rho_1^\sigma(y,\ell) \ell \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} (y \sqrt{1-t}) \,\mathrm{d} \ell \,\mathrm{d} y \,\mathrm{d} t \\ & \qquad + \int_{-\infty}^\infty \int_0^1 \int_{-\infty}^\infty \int_0^\infty \frac{|x| e^{-\frac{x^2}{2 (\sigma(x))^2}}}{\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma(x)} \sqrt{\frac{1}t-1} \rho_1^\sigma(y,\ell) \ell h(x \sqrt{t},y \sqrt{1-t}) \,\mathrm{d} \ell \,\mathrm{d} y \,\mathrm{d} t \lambda_\sigma(\!\,\mathrm{d} x) \end{split}\end{equation} where $\rho_1^\sigma$ is the joint density of a standard OBM and its local time at time $1$ (given in \eqref{eq:OBMl}). This expression can be easily checked to be the desired expression for $c_h$.
nodes.section: C.4 Dealing with the martingale term
nodes.statement_short: Conditional variances converge to $K_h^Y L_t(Y)$ by Proposition 7.

nodes.name: First step
nodes.statement: {\it First step:} It can be easily shown that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \sqrt n \mathbb{E}\!\left[ (\chi_k^n)^2 | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & = f_{n}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) + (\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle)^2 \Lm{1}{2}{\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}} - 2 \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle h_n(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) \end{split} \end{equation} where $f_n$ and $h_n$ are given by $ f_n(x) := \bfH {h^2}(x) + 2 \bfH{h, \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}} (x) + g_n(x) $ and $ h_n(x):= \Lm{h(x, \cdot)}{1}{x} + \Lm{\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}}{1}{x}, $ with $ g_n(x):=Q^\sigma_1\left( ( \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0} )^2 \right) (x) - \left(\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(x)\right)^2 $. In fact first note that, by \eqref{function:G:equal}, for all $k =1, \ldots, {\lfloor n t \rfloor}$ it holds that \begin{equation} h_n(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k-1}{n}})= \sqrt{n} \mathbb{E}\Big[ (h(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k-1}{n}}, \sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k}{n}}) + \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k}{n}}) ) (L_{\frac{k}{n}}(Y) - L_{\frac{k-1}n}(Y)) | \mathcal{F}_{\frac{k-1}n}\Big] . \end{equation} Let us now consider $f_n$. Clearly $f_n$ have to be the sum of all remaining terms and it has to have the desired form. This follows from the fact that the scaling property~\eqref{Yscaling} and equation~\eqref{eq:cQ} ensure that $\mathbb{E}\Big[ (\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{k/n}))^2 | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\Big] = Q^\sigma_1 ( (\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{k/n}))^2 ). $ but also $\mathbb{E}\Big[ \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{k/n}) | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\Big] = \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(\sqrt n Y_{(k-1)/n})$ which, together with the definition of $\bfG{h}$ in \eqref{eq:kappa}, \eqref{function:G:equal}, and the fact that $ \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) = \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) - \bfG{h}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) $ show that $\mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n})$ can be rewritten as \begin{equation} \begin{split} \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,1}(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k-1}{n}}) = \mathbb{E}\Big[ h(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k-1}n}, \sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k}{n}}) + \mathcal{Q}_{n,0,0}(\sqrt{n} Y_{\frac{k}n}) -\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle \sqrt{n} ( L_{\frac{k}n}(Y) - L_{\frac{k-1}n}(Y) ) | \mathcal{F}_{\frac{k-1}n}\Big] . \end{split} \end{equation} The proof of the first step is thus completed.

nodes.name: Equation (C.30)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} & c_h = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{(\sigma_- + \sigma_+)}{2\sigma_-\sigma_+} \int_0^1 \sqrt{\frac{1}t-1} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \int_0^\infty \rho_1^\sigma(y,\ell) \ell \mathcal{P}_{h}^{Y} (y \sqrt{1-t}) \,\mathrm{d} \ell \,\mathrm{d} y \,\mathrm{d} t \\ & \qquad + \int_{-\infty}^\infty \int_0^1 \int_{-\infty}^\infty \int_0^\infty \frac{|x| e^{-\frac{x^2}{2 (\sigma(x))^2}}}{\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma(x)} \sqrt{\frac{1}t-1} \rho_1^\sigma(y,\ell) \ell h(x \sqrt{t},y \sqrt{1-t}) \,\mathrm{d} \ell \,\mathrm{d} y \,\mathrm{d} t \lambda_\sigma(\!\,\mathrm{d} x) \end{split}

nodes.name: Item (iii)
nodes.statement: Let $t\in [0,1]$ be fixed. {\it First step:} Let us show that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[\chi_k^n (Y_{k/n} - Y_{(k-1)/n}) | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & = \frac1{\sqrt n} \left( n^{-\frac14} f_1(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) + g_{n}(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) + \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle n^{-\frac14} f_2(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n})\right) \end{split} \end{equation} where $f_1,f_2,g_n$ are given by \begin{equation} \begin{split} f_1(x)& := \int_{-\infty}^\infty (h(x,y)+\bfG{h}(y)) (y-x) q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y , \ f_2(x):= x \Lm{1}{1}{x}, \ \text{and} \\ g_n(x) & := n^{-\frac14} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}(y) (y-x) q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y. \end{split} \end{equation} Throughout the proof of this step let $\mathbb{Id} \colon x\mapsto x$ denote the identity function. It follows from \eqref{eq:chi:nk}, the fact that $Y$ is a martingale, \eqref{function:G:equal}, and the scaling property~\eqref{Yscaling} that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & n^{\frac34} \, \mathbb{E}\!\left[\chi_k^n (Y_{k/n} - Y_{(k-1)/n}) | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & = f_1(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) + \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle f_2(\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}) - \Lm{ \mathbb{Id} }{1}{\sqrt{n} Y_{(k-1)/n}} ) + n^{1/4}g_n(\sqrt{n}Y_{(k-1)/n}). \end{split} \end{equation} The proof of this step is completed if $ \Lm{ \mathbb{Id} }{1}{\cdot} =0$. This equality follows from the fact that for a standard BM, say $W$, it holds that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[ L_1(W) W_1 \right]=0$ and from Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:G}. In the next steps we want to check that Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1a:j1} can be applied to the sequences $n^{-\frac14} f_1$, $n^{-\frac14} f_2$ and $g_n$. {\it Second step:} We show that $f_1$ is bounded and integrable: $f_1\in \Lgb{0}$. The proof follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa}, and Item~\ref{item2bis:semig:estim} in Lemma~\ref{lem:semig:estim}. In this proof the fact that $\gamma>3$ is strongly used. The fact that $h\in \Lg{\gamma}\subseteq \Lg{3}$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa} ensure that $\bar h$ and $\bfG{h}$ are in $\Lgb{2}$. This, Cauchy-Schwarz, the fact that $ \left(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (y-x)^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right) \leq \sigma_-^2 \ind{\{\sigma_-\in\mathbb{R}\}} +\sigma_+^2 \ind{\{\sigma_+\in\mathbb{R}\}} $, and the fact that that $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (\bfG{h}(y))^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y = Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)$ yield \begin{equation} \begin{split} |f_1(x)| & \leq \bar h(x) \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{a |y-x|} |y-x| q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y + \sqrt{\sigma_-^2 \ind{\{\sigma_-\in\mathbb{R}\}} +\sigma_+^2 \ind{\{\sigma_+\in\mathbb{R}\}}} \left( |Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)| \right)^{\!1/2}. \end{split} \end{equation} By Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa} $\bfG{h}$ is bounded, i.e.~there exists $K\in (0,\infty)$ such that $\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}}|\bfG{h}(x)|\leq K$ and $\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfG{h} \rangle=0 $, and so $ | \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfG{h}^2 \rangle | \leq K | \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfG{h} \rangle | =0. $ And so Item~\ref{item2bis:semig:estim} in Lemma~\ref{lem:semig:estim} implies, up to increase the constant $K\in [1,\infty)$, that \begin{equation} |Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)| \leq K \frac{1}{1+|x/\sigma(x)|^{\gamma-1}} + K \frac1{\sqrt{2 \pi}} e^{-\frac{x^2}{2 (\sigma(x))^2 }} \leq 2 K^2 \frac{1}{(1+|x/\sigma(x)|^{\frac{\gamma-1}{2}})^2} . \end{equation} Since $\gamma >3 $ it holds that $\left( |Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)| \right)^{\!\frac12}\in \Lgb{0}$ and so $|f_1|\in \Lgb{0}$. {\it Third step:} The fact that $f_2$ is bounded and integrable follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:G}. This and the change of variable $s \mapsto r= \frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2 s}$ show that there exists a positive constant $K$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} f_2(x) & = \left(\frac{2 \sigma_-\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right)^{\! 2} \frac{x |x|}{\sigma(x)} \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \frac{L_1(W)}{\sigma(W_1)} \right] \int_0^1 \frac{\sqrt{1-s}}{\sqrt{2\pi} s^\frac32} e^{-\frac{x^2}{2 (\sigma(x))^2 s}} \! \,\mathrm{d} s \\ & = \left(\frac{2 \sigma_-\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right)^{\! 2} \frac{x |x|}{\sigma(x)} \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \frac{L_1(W)}{\sigma(W_1)} \right] \int_{\frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2}}^\infty \frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}} \sqrt{\frac{(\sigma(x))^2}{x^2}-\frac1r} e^{-\frac{r}{2}} \frac1{\sqrt{r}}\! \,\mathrm{d} r \ \ind{\{\sigma(x)\in \mathbb{R}\}} \\ & \leq \left(\frac{2 \sigma_-\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right)^{\! 2} \frac{|x| \mathbb{E}\!\left[L_1(W)\right] }{\min\{\sigma_-,\sigma_+\}} \int_{\frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2}}^\infty \frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{r}{2}} \frac1{\sqrt{r}}\! \,\mathrm{d} r \ \ind{\{\sigma(x)\in \mathbb{R}\}} \leq K e^{-\frac{x^2}{4(\sigma(x))^2}} \in \Lgb{0}. \end{split} \end{equation} In the last inequality we used that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[ L_1(W) \right] \in [0,\infty)$. This step is thus completed. {\it Fourth step:} We prove that $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |g_n(x)| \,\mathrm{d} x$ and $\frac1{\sqrt{n}} g_n(\sqrt{n} x)$ converge to 0. Cauchy-Schwarz inequality ensures \begin{equation} \begin{split} |g_n(x)|^2 & \leq n^{-1/2} \left( \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}(y))^2 q_\sigma (1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right) \left(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (y-x)^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right). \end{split} \end{equation} Note that $ \left(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (y-x)^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right) \leq \sigma_-^2 \ind{\{\sigma_-\in \mathbb{R}\}} +\sigma_+^2 \ind{\{\sigma_+\in \mathbb{R}\}} $ and inequality~\eqref{eq:recicle} yield that there exists a constant $K\in (0,\infty)$ depending on $\gamma$ and $\sigma_\pm$ such that $ |g_n(x)| \leq \frac{n^{-\frac14} K_2 \log (n)}{1+|x n^{-\frac18}/\sigma(x)|^{\gamma-1}}. $ In the last steps we proved that Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1a:j1} can be applied and this completes the proof.

nodes.statement_short: Covariation with $Y$ vanishes by Proposition 6.

nodes.name: First step

The proof follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa}, and Item~\ref{item2bis:semig:estim} in Lemma~\ref{lem:semig:estim}. In this proof the fact that $\gamma>3$ is strongly used. The fact that $h\in \Lg{\gamma}\subseteq \Lg{3}$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa} ensure that $\bar h$ and $\bfG{h}$ are in $\Lgb{2}$. This, Cauchy-Schwarz, the fact that $ \left(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (y-x)^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right) \leq \sigma_-^2 \ind{\{\sigma_-\in\mathbb{R}\}} +\sigma_+^2 \ind{\{\sigma_+\in\mathbb{R}\}} $, and the fact that that $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (\bfG{h}(y))^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y = Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)$ yield \begin{equation} \begin{split} |f_1(x)| & \leq \bar h(x) \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{a |y-x|} |y-x| q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y + \sqrt{\sigma_-^2 \ind{\{\sigma_-\in\mathbb{R}\}} +\sigma_+^2 \ind{\{\sigma_+\in\mathbb{R}\}}} \left( |Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)| \right)^{\!1/2}. \end{split} \end{equation} By Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:kappa} $\bfG{h}$ is bounded, i.e.~there exists $K\in (0,\infty)$ such that $\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}}|\bfG{h}(x)|\leq K$ and $\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfG{h} \rangle=0 $, and so $ | \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfG{h}^2 \rangle | \leq K | \langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfG{h} \rangle | =0. $ And so Item~\ref{item2bis:semig:estim} in Lemma~\ref{lem:semig:estim} implies, up to increase the constant $K\in [1,\infty)$, that \begin{equation} |Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)| \leq K \frac{1}{1+|x/\sigma(x)|^{\gamma-1}} + K \frac1{\sqrt{2 \pi}} e^{-\frac{x^2}{2 (\sigma(x))^2 }} \leq 2 K^2 \frac{1}{(1+|x/\sigma(x)|^{\frac{\gamma-1}{2}})^2} . \end{equation} Since $\gamma >3 $ it holds that $\left( |Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)| \right)^{\!\frac12}\in \Lgb{0}$ and so $|f_1|\in \Lgb{0}$.

nodes.name: Equation (C.34)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} |f_1(x)| & \leq \bar h(x) \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{a |y-x|} |y-x| q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y + \sqrt{\sigma_-^2 \ind{\{\sigma_-\in\mathbb{R}\}} +\sigma_+^2 \ind{\{\sigma_+\in\mathbb{R}\}}} \left( |Q^\sigma_1 \bfG{h}^2 (x)| \right)^{\!1/2}. \end{split}

nodes.name: Third step
nodes.statement: {\it Third step:} The fact that $f_2$ is bounded and integrable follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:G}. This and the change of variable $s \mapsto r= \frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2 s}$ show that there exists a positive constant $K$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} f_2(x) & = \left(\frac{2 \sigma_-\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right)^{\! 2} \frac{x |x|}{\sigma(x)} \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \frac{L_1(W)}{\sigma(W_1)} \right] \int_0^1 \frac{\sqrt{1-s}}{\sqrt{2\pi} s^\frac32} e^{-\frac{x^2}{2 (\sigma(x))^2 s}} \! \,\mathrm{d} s \\ & = \left(\frac{2 \sigma_-\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right)^{\! 2} \frac{x |x|}{\sigma(x)} \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \frac{L_1(W)}{\sigma(W_1)} \right] \int_{\frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2}}^\infty \frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}} \sqrt{\frac{(\sigma(x))^2}{x^2}-\frac1r} e^{-\frac{r}{2}} \frac1{\sqrt{r}}\! \,\mathrm{d} r \ \ind{\{\sigma(x)\in \mathbb{R}\}} \\ & \leq \left(\frac{2 \sigma_-\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right)^{\! 2} \frac{|x| \mathbb{E}\!\left[L_1(W)\right] }{\min\{\sigma_-,\sigma_+\}} \int_{\frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2}}^\infty \frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{r}{2}} \frac1{\sqrt{r}}\! \,\mathrm{d} r \ \ind{\{\sigma(x)\in \mathbb{R}\}} \leq K e^{-\frac{x^2}{4(\sigma(x))^2}} \in \Lgb{0}. \end{split} \end{equation} In the last inequality we used that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[ L_1(W) \right] \in [0,\infty)$. This step is thus completed.
nodes.section: C.4 Dealing with the martingale term
nodes.statement_short: $f_2$ bounded and integrable via Lemma 6.

nodes.name: Equation (C.36)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} f_2(x) & = \left(\frac{2 \sigma_-\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right)^{\! 2} \frac{x |x|}{\sigma(x)} \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \frac{L_1(W)}{\sigma(W_1)} \right] \int_0^1 \frac{\sqrt{1-s}}{\sqrt{2\pi} s^\frac32} e^{-\frac{x^2}{2 (\sigma(x))^2 s}} \! \,\mathrm{d} s \\ & = \left(\frac{2 \sigma_-\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right)^{\! 2} \frac{x |x|}{\sigma(x)} \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \frac{L_1(W)}{\sigma(W_1)} \right] \int_{\frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2}}^\infty \frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}} \sqrt{\frac{(\sigma(x))^2}{x^2}-\frac1r} e^{-\frac{r}{2}} \frac1{\sqrt{r}}\! \,\mathrm{d} r \ \ind{\{\sigma(x)\in \mathbb{R}\}} \\ & \leq \left(\frac{2 \sigma_-\sigma_+}{\sigma_-+\sigma_+}\right)^{\! 2} \frac{|x| \mathbb{E}\!\left[L_1(W)\right] }{\min\{\sigma_-,\sigma_+\}} \int_{\frac{x^2}{(\sigma(x))^2}}^\infty \frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{r}{2}} \frac1{\sqrt{r}}\! \,\mathrm{d} r \ \ind{\{\sigma(x)\in \mathbb{R}\}} \leq K e^{-\frac{x^2}{4(\sigma(x))^2}} \in \Lgb{0}. \end{split}

nodes.name: Fourth step
nodes.statement: {\it Fourth step:} We prove that $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |g_n(x)| \,\mathrm{d} x$ and $\frac1{\sqrt{n}} g_n(\sqrt{n} x)$ converge to 0. Cauchy-Schwarz inequality ensures \begin{equation} \begin{split} |g_n(x)|^2 & \leq n^{-1/2} \left( \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}(y))^2 q_\sigma (1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right) \left(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (y-x)^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right). \end{split} \end{equation} Note that $ \left(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (y-x)^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right) \leq \sigma_-^2 \ind{\{\sigma_-\in \mathbb{R}\}} +\sigma_+^2 \ind{\{\sigma_+\in \mathbb{R}\}} $ and inequality~\eqref{eq:recicle} yield that there exists a constant $K\in (0,\infty)$ depending on $\gamma$ and $\sigma_\pm$ such that $ |g_n(x)| \leq \frac{n^{-\frac14} K_2 \log (n)}{1+|x n^{-\frac18}/\sigma(x)|^{\gamma-1}}. $ In the last steps we proved that Proposition~\ref{prop:th4.1a:j1} can be applied and this completes the proof.
nodes.section: C.4 Dealing with the martingale term
nodes.statement_short: $g_n$ vanishes in $L^1$; Proposition 6 applies.

nodes.name: Equation (C.37)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} |g_n(x)|^2 & \leq n^{-1/2} \left( \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (\mathcal{Q}_{n,1,0}(y))^2 q_\sigma (1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right) \left(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (y-x)^2 q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y\right). \end{split}
nodes.section: C.4.3 Proof of Item~th:j2:item3:2 in Proposition~4

nodes.name: Item (iv)
nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon \in (0,\infty)$ be fixed. For every $k$, H\"older's inequality and Markov's inequality show \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[ |\chi_k^n|^2 \ind{\{|\chi_k^n|\geq \varepsilon \}}| \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \leq \mathbb{E}\!\left[ |\chi_k^n|^{5} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \varepsilon^{-3} . \end{split} \end{equation} The fact that $h\in \Lg{\gamma}\subseteq \Lg{0}$ ensures that $\bar h$ is bounded and integrable. This combined with Jensen's inequality and \eqref{eq:cQ:prop4} ensures that $\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}} \bar h(x) + |\langle \lambda_\sigma , \bfH h \rangle| $ is bounded by a constant $K\in (0,\infty)$ and for all $n\in \mathbb{N}\setminus\{0,1,2,3\}$ it holds that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[ |\chi_k^n|^{5} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \leq 4^{4} n^{-\frac{5}{4}} K^{5} \Big( \mathbb{E}\!\left[ e^{5 a \sqrt n | Y_{k/n} - Y_{(k-1)/n}|} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & \quad \qquad + \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \left(\sqrt{n}|L_{k/n}(Y) - L_{(k-1)/n}(Y)| \right)^{5} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] + (\log n)^{5} \Big). \end{split} \end{equation} The fact that density of the OBM has a Gaussian behavior together with the scaling property~\eqref{Yscaling} ensure that $ \mathbb{E}\!\left[ e^{5 a \sqrt n | Y_{k/n} - Y_{(k-1)/n}|} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{5 a |y-x|} q_\sigma(1,x,y) \,\mathrm{d} y $ is bounded. By \eqref{function:G} and Lemma~\ref{lem:prop:G} we can show, similarly to the third step of the proof of Item~\ref{th:j2:item3}, that there exist constants $K_1,K_2 \in (0,\infty)$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \left(\sqrt{n}|L_{k/n}(Y) - L_{(k-1)/n}(Y)| \right)^{5} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] = \Lm {1}{5}{\sqrt{n}Y_{(k-1)/n}} \\ & \leq K_1 \int_0^1 \frac{(1-t)^{\frac52}}{\sqrt{2 \pi} t^{\frac32}} \frac{\sqrt{n}|Y_{(k-1)/n}|}{\sigma(Y_{(k-1)/n})} e^{-\frac{n (Y_{(k-1)/n})^2}{2 (\sigma(Y_{(k-1)/n})) t } } \,\mathrm{d} t \leq K_2. \end{split} \end{equation} We conclude that there exists a constant $K\in (0,\infty)$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \sum_{k=1}^n \mathbb{E}\!\left[ |\chi_k^n|^2 \ind{\{|\chi_k^n|\geq \varepsilon \}}| \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \leq n K n^{-\frac54} \log(n) \varepsilon^{-3} \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{} 0. \end{split} \end{equation}
nodes.section: C.4 Dealing with the martingale term
nodes.statement_short: Lindeberg condition via fifth moments, Markov's inequality and Lemma 6.

nodes.name: Equation (C.38)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[ |\chi_k^n|^2 \ind{\{|\chi_k^n|\geq \varepsilon \}}| \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \leq \mathbb{E}\!\left[ |\chi_k^n|^{5} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \varepsilon^{-3} . \end{split}
nodes.section: C.4.4 Proof of Item~th:j2:item4:2 in Proposition~4

nodes.name: Equation (C.39)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[ |\chi_k^n|^{5} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \leq 4^{4} n^{-\frac{5}{4}} K^{5} \Big( \mathbb{E}\!\left[ e^{5 a \sqrt n | Y_{k/n} - Y_{(k-1)/n}|} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \\ & \quad \qquad + \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \left(\sqrt{n}|L_{k/n}(Y) - L_{(k-1)/n}(Y)| \right)^{5} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] + (\log n)^{5} \Big). \end{split}
nodes.section: C.4.4 Proof of Item~th:j2:item4:2 in Proposition~4

nodes.name: Equation (C.40)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} & \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \left(\sqrt{n}|L_{k/n}(Y) - L_{(k-1)/n}(Y)| \right)^{5} | \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] = \Lm {1}{5}{\sqrt{n}Y_{(k-1)/n}} \\ & \leq K_1 \int_0^1 \frac{(1-t)^{\frac52}}{\sqrt{2 \pi} t^{\frac32}} \frac{\sqrt{n}|Y_{(k-1)/n}|}{\sigma(Y_{(k-1)/n})} e^{-\frac{n (Y_{(k-1)/n})^2}{2 (\sigma(Y_{(k-1)/n})) t } } \,\mathrm{d} t \leq K_2. \end{split}
nodes.section: C.4.4 Proof of Item~th:j2:item4:2 in Proposition~4

nodes.name: Equation (C.41)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} & \sum_{k=1}^n \mathbb{E}\!\left[ |\chi_k^n|^2 \ind{\{|\chi_k^n|\geq \varepsilon \}}| \mathcal{F}_{(k-1)/n}\right] \leq n K n^{-\frac54} \log(n) \varepsilon^{-3} \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{} 0. \end{split}
nodes.section: C.4.4 Proof of Item~th:j2:item4:2 in Proposition~4
